description: Know how many agents each interval needs — and where your roster falls short. Charting contact volume in Power BI is easy. Turning it into a defensible staffing requirement is not. Erlang C is awkward to write in DAX, spreadsheet macros are fragile, Python visuals bring deployment and refresh problems, and sending your contact data to an external calculator is a procurement conversation nobody wants. This visual does the calculation inside Power BI, on your machine. WHAT IT TELLS YOU • Required productive agents per interval, from Erlang C • Required scheduled agents after shrinkage • The gap against your actual roster, interval by interval • The service level your roster is forecast to deliver • Expected occupancy, enforced against a ceiling you set BUILT FOR HOW STAFFING ACTUALLY WORKS • Maximum occupancy is a hard constraint, not a footnote. Sustained occupancy above roughly 85% drives burnout and attrition. Calculators that only target service level can hand you an answer implying 90% occupancy or higher. This one will not, unless you raise the ceiling yourself. • Shrinkage is applied where it belongs — after the Erlang C calculation, never folded into offered load. • Every number is reconcilable. The tooltip shows the whole chain: offered load in Erlangs, required productive agents, required scheduled agents. Check any interval against your own spreadsheet. NUMERICALLY…
